what: Russian artist and Putin critic shot dead in Poland

clean_source_blocks.text: Police in Poland are investigating the murder of a Russian artist and vocal critic of President Vladimir Putin. Polish prosecutors said Robert K, known as the artist Semyon Skrepetsky, was shot dead on Monday morning in the Polish town of Biała Podlaska, about 40km (25 miles) from the Belarusian border. The 44-year-old was shot five times in the head, chest and back in a car park in the town, located about 600m (2,000ft) from the Belarusian consulate. Semyon Skrepetsky was the pseudonym used by Robert Kuzovkov. He was known for his caricatures of politicians, including Putin, Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko and Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov.

A Russian artist known for criticizing President Vladimir Putin with his caricatures was shot dead execution-style in Poland, local prosecutors said Tuesday. Kremlin opposition figure Robert Kuzovkov, also known by his artistic name Semyon Skrepetsky, was first shot twice Monday morning by the gunman who approached him in the eastern Polish town of Biala Podlaska near the Belarusian border, according to officials and local media. "When the victim fell to the ground, the perpetrator approached, fired three more shots and then quickly fled the scene," said Marcin Kozak, a spokesperson for the District Prosecutor's Office in Lublin. At least one of the five shots was to the head. "Robert K. died at the scene," Kozak confirmed. Two Belarusians were detained, but have not been charged. It's unclear what role they might have had in the shooting.
Robert Kuzovkov, who used the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, has been known for his caricatures of politicians including Vladimir Putin.

A Russian artist well-known for satirising President Vladimir Putin has been shot dead in eastern Poland, officials said on Tuesday. "An investigation is being conducted...into the murder of a 44-year-old citizen of the Russian Federation...known in the media as Semyon Skrepetsky," a spokesman for the prosecutor's office in Lublin, Marcin Kozak, told journalists. Two Belarusian nationals have been arrested in connection with the killing, he added. They were detained in the vicinity of the Belarusian consulate in Biała Podlaska in eastern Poland, where the killing took place. According to Polish officials, Skrepetsky, whose real name is Robert Kuzovkov, was shot three times on Monday morning by an unidentified gunman armed with a handgun. When the artist fell to the ground, he was approached by the assailant, who fired two more shots at close range.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Police in Poland are investigating the murder of a Russian artist and vocal critic of President Vladimir Putin.

Polish prosecutors said Robert K, known as the artist Semyon Skrepetsky, was shot dead on Monday morning in the Polish town of Biała Podlaska, about 40km (25 miles) from the Belarusian border.

The 44-year-old was shot five times in the head, chest and back in a car park in the town, located about 600m (2,000ft) from the Belarusian consulate.

Semyon Skrepetsky was the pseudonym used by Robert Kuzovkov. He was known for his caricatures of politicians, including Putin, Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko and Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov.

Police have detained two Belarusian citizens, aged 33 and 37, near the Belarusian consulate in the town and their role in the incident is still being determined, says Marcin Kozak, spokesman for the district prosecutor's office in the eastern city of Lublin.

Skrepetsky was given asylum in Biała Podlaska, a small town with a population of less than 60,000, after he left Russia in 2021 fearing criminal prosecution.

Kozak said the artist was approached by an unidentified gunman who fired two shots at him.

"When the victim fell to the ground, the perpetrator approached, fired three more shots and then quickly fled the scene. Robert K died at the scene," he added.

Five shell casings and one Geco 9mm Luger bullet were recovered from the crime scene, Kozak said.

A post mortem examination has been scheduled for Wednesday.

Belarusian artist Vladislav Bokhan, who knew Skrepetsky, said he had found out about the shooting from Polish radio and immediately felt concerned: "I thought, that's where Skrepetsky lives. I know it's a very small town."

"The victim engaged in public artistic activities and used among other things, the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, under which he expressed criticism of the current policies of the Russian Federation authorities," Kozak said.

Skrepetsky's satirical cartoons had depicted Putin in the arms of Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin, Lukashenko as Adolf Hitler with a bucket of potatoes and Kadyrov and his son Adam with pigs' snouts.

He had also mocked Russian opposition figure Alexei Navalny as well as ordinary Ukrainians and his Polish address was freely available online. His work was posted on Telegram and on his YouTube channel.

Skrepetsky is survived in Poland by his wife and five children.

The 44-year-old artist was murdered three days after he joined a protest in Berlin on Russia Day, which celebrates the country declaring sovereignty before the Soviet Union collapsed, the news outlet Meduza reported.

He hoisted a painting that caricatured Putin and Soviet strongman Joseph Stalin, and also wore a Russian flag tied to his pants that dragged along the road outside the Russian embassy, the BCC reported.

"The victim engaged in public artistic activities and used among other things, the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, under which he expressed criticism of the current policies of the Russian Federation authorities," said Kozak, the prosecutor's office spokesperson.

Poland has been a central point for military and other supplies for Ukraine as Kyiv's war with Moscow drags on.

That role has made the nation a target for Russian spies, according to Polish officials.

The Russian embassy was not immediately available for comment.

A spokesperson for Poland's special services minister said the Internal Security Agency is cooperating with police and prosecutors involved in the investigation.

payload.title: Putinia arvostellut venäläistaiteilija ammuttiin Puolassa
payload.summary: Puolan viranomaiset tutkivat venäläistaiteilija Robert Kuzovkovin surmaa Biała Podlaskan kaupungissa lähellä Valko-Venäjän rajaa. Kuzovkov tunnettiin taiteilijanimellä Semyon Skrepetsky ja poliitikkoja arvostelevista pilapiirroksistaan.
payload.content:
Venäläinen taiteilija ja presidentti Vladimir Putinin näkyvä arvostelija Robert Kuzovkov on ammuttu kuoliaaksi Itä-Puolassa. Puolan syyttäjien mukaan 44-vuotias Kuzovkov, joka tunnettiin taiteilijanimellä Semyon Skrepetsky, kuoli maanantaiaamuna Biała Podlaskan kaupungissa lähellä Valko-Venäjän rajaa, ja viranomaiset tutkivat tapausta henkirikoksena.

## Ampuminen tapahtui pysäköintialueella

Puolan viranomaisten mukaan Kuzovkov ammuttiin pysäköintialueella Biała Podlaskassa. Kaupunki sijaitsee noin 40 kilometrin päässä Valko-Venäjän rajasta, ja tapahtumapaikan on kerrottu olleen noin 600 metrin päässä Valko-Venäjän konsulaatista.

Lublinin alueellisen syyttäjänviraston edustaja Marcin Kozak on kuvannut ampumista vaiheittaiseksi hyökkäykseksi. Hänen mukaansa tekijä lähestyi uhria ja ampui tätä ensin. Kun Kuzovkov kaatui maahan, ampuja tuli lähemmäs ja ampui vielä useita laukauksia lähietäisyydeltä ennen kuin pakeni paikalta.

Viranomaisten mukaan Kuzovkov sai yhteensä viisi osumaa päähän, rintaan ja selkään. Ainakin yhden laukauksen on kerrottu osuneen päähän. Kozakin mukaan Kuzovkov kuoli tapahtumapaikalla.

## Kaksi Valko-Venäjän kansalaista otettu kiinni

Tapaukseen liittyen on otettu kiinni kaksi Valko-Venäjän kansalaista. Heidät pidätettiin Biała Podlaskassa Valko-Venäjän konsulaatin läheisyydessä. Lähdetietojen mukaan heitä ei ole kuitenkaan syytetty, eikä heidän mahdollista rooliaan ampumisessa ole vahvistettu.

Viranomaiset eivät ole nimenneet epäiltyä ampujaa julkisuuteen. Myöskään teon motiivista ei ole kerrottu vahvistettua tietoa.

## Kuzovkov tunnettiin poliittisista pilapiirroksista

Kuzovkov käytti taiteilijanimeä Semyon Skrepetsky. Hänet tunnettiin poliittisista pilapiirroksista, joissa hän käsitteli muun muassa Venäjän presidenttiä Vladimir Putinia, Valko-Venäjän johtajaa Aljaksandr Lukašenkaa ja Tšetšenian johtajaa Ramzan Kadyrovia.

Puolan viranomaisten mukaan tutkinta jatkuu. Julkisuuteen kerrotut tiedot eivät vielä vahvista, liittyikö surma Kuzovkovin poliittiseen taiteeseen tai hänen julkiseen arvosteluunsa Venäjän johtoa kohtaan.
summary_bullets: Venäläistaiteilija Robert Kuzovkov ammuttiin kuoliaaksi Itä-Puolassa maanantaiaamuna.
Kuzovkov tunnettiin taiteilijanimellä Semyon Skrepetsky ja Putinin sekä muiden johtajien pilapiirroksista.
Puolan viranomaiset ovat ottaneet kiinni kaksi Valko-Venäjän kansalaista, mutta heidän rooliaan ei ole vahvistettu.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketin yhteneviin tietoihin Puolan viranomaisten tutkinnasta, uhrin henkilöllisyydestä, tapahtumapaikasta ja kiinniotoista. Motiivia tai kiinniotettujen roolia ei ole vahvistettu, joten ne on rajattu avoimiksi.
